title: Road manager Frenchie, the band doctor and subleaders McRae and Garland
summary: Armstrong delegated hiring to subleaders; Frenchie handled travel and pay, Teddy McRae then Joe Garland led rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: On this tour, Louie always carried a doctor and a road manager. Whenever anybody got sick, we had the band doctor and a guy by the name of Frenchie was the road manager, he arranged transportation and hotels, paid off the boys. Many nights we got money before we even went to work because he'd get it in cash and distribute it before the job. That's the way Louie operated the band. He never did the hiring and the firing, he always left it to a sub-leader who rehearsed the band music and rehearsed the

arrangements behind him all through his tour where he would be studying on his lyrics. Then when he'd warm up he'd get a mouthpiece and just blow it, just to get warmed up before he performed.
Who was the subleader there, Ed Mullens or was it Teddy McRae?

When I first joined the band it was Teddy McRae and then Teddy had something else there to do and then Joe Garland took over. It was Joe Garland who is on these records, Joe Garland supervised that recording session. Louie was just there to just play his parts and soloed; but Joe Garland was in charge of the band then.
